feedback.problem: Given that $p(x)={x}^{2}$ and $q(x)=-7{x}^{4},$ what is ${lim}_{x\to \infty }\frac{{x}^{2}\cdot p(x)}{q(x)}?$
feedback.worked_solution:
First, let's calculate ${x}^{2}\cdot p(x):$

$$
{x}^{2}\cdot p(x)={x}^{2}\cdot {x}^{2}={x}^{4}.
$$

When we divide the two functions ${x}^{2}\cdot p(x)$ and $q(x),$ we get a constant, and the limit of a constant is just the constant itself:

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to \infty }\frac{{x}^{2}\cdot p(x)}{q(x)} & ={lim}_{x\to \infty }\frac{{x}^{4}}{(-7{x}^{4})} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to \infty }-\frac{1}{7} \\  & =-\frac{1}{7}\end{aligned}
$$
